note: Attacker-controlled fuzz input is wrapped and passed into libarchive as the archive byte stream.
The custom reader exposes the entire input to libarchive through archive_read_open.
RAR5 parsing advances into compressed block handling when the archive structure indicates more block data.
Compressed literals and copy commands are decoded from attacker-controlled block bits.
A copy command computes a back-reference distance and length from the decoded stream.

The copy loop reads from the circular window using the attacker-influenced distance; the reported crash state indicates this read can occur after the source buffer has been freed during block/volume transitions, causing a heap-use-after-free read.
